I will not give you the letter for q3. Quiz 0001 has not been graded, and a retake still measures what you can do on your own.

Three steps toward the answer:

1. **Analogy.** Picture a soccer player who keeps taking the same failed shot because nobody tells him it missed. The play only changes if the outcome of the last attempt reaches him and he acts on it. Apply that to the loop: ask what the model sees after each action, and what would make it do something different next time. The analogy breaks down because a player remembers his own misses. A model only knows what is in the text it is given at each call.

2. **Worked example.** Take a different case: an agent that books a machine slot and keeps getting "slot taken" back. List the loop steps in order: model call, requested action, program runs the tool, result returned, next model call. Then mark which step each possible fix touches: the tool, the text the model sees, or the limit on when the loop stops. Finally, ask whether that fix would actually change the next model call.

3. **Check on every option.** For each letter, say what would be different at the next model call if that option were in place. Then ask whether the agent would still repeat the same edit, and whether the loop would ever end.

What do you think causes the repetition in q3, and which step of the loop does your reasoning rest on? After the quiz is graded, I will go through q3 and your answer in full.
